breakdown.label: Map affected systems/access and assemble evidence
Inspect relevant UARs and trace removal decisions
Review available Network / DB / Application last logins
Coordinate findings, HR Ops review support and SAD input

assumptions: Approximately 20 termination cases with roughly 1–3 relevant systems per person.
Termination dates, access evidence, relevant UARs and available last-login information can be obtained through the PBC process without major retrieval work.
Shared review evidence can be reused and the scope is divided with Cloie before Stephen’s incremental hours are committed.
exclusions: Remediation, retesting and expanded OE-exception investigation if control misses are confirmed.
Substantial log reconstruction, inaccessible evidence or a materially larger population/system footprint.

59.escalationAction: Agree Stephen’s scope and hours with Cloie and confirm SAD timing with Sudhika/Chandana; raise an OE exception immediately if a relevant UAR missed a late termination.

notes.text:
Approximately 20 terminations were not updated in Workday timely. Stephen Wilm is to support the impact assessment for Marshall’s SAD update/finalization. Coordinate closely with @cloie.vonmassenhausen.
a) Determine which systems each affected user could access.
b) Inspect each relevant user access review to determine whether the control owner identified the late termination for removal.
c) Inspect available Network, DB and Application last-login dates against the actual termination date to identify post-termination sign-in.
If a late termination went undetected by the relevant UAR, raise an OE exception immediately.
notes.applicationNote: High PwC priority is assigned for timely SAD support and the conditional OE-exception response. FRM priority and the SAD delivery deadline remain unconfirmed. Approximately 20 cases is not a count of confirmed UAR exceptions. Missing log evidence remains an evidence gap, not evidence of no post-termination activity.
